method.rust: RUSTFLAGS=-C instrument-coverage; cargo +nightly test -p ffmpeg --lib --tests -- --skip compile_fail refstruct frame buffer; nightly llvm-profdata merge + llvm-cov export -summary-only over the lib, equiv, ub_safe and ub_unsafe binaries, reported for the three homes (whole files, so the wave-0 and wave-1 type items in them are included)
method.c: the same run with CRUSTIFY_FFMPEG_VARIANT=coverage and GCOV_PREFIX; gcov 13 -b -c -f over refstruct.c, side_data.c and buffer.c (gcc 14 build; gcov warns about the version, and its line percentages can exceed 100 for functions with inlined bodies, as refstruct_pool_get_ext), reported for the workset functions and the static helpers they run
method.note: measured on the landed tree (wave tip 6fd5597711 plus this review). C: every line of the workset functions runs except av_refstruct_pool_alloc_ext_c:382-383, the ff_mutex_init failure branch, which glibc never takes. Rust: refstruct.rs misses line 395 (the pool up-ref refusal on a narrow count, unreachable on the 64-bit host), 898 (release_with when CSliceMut::into_mut(0) of a one-element slice is None) and 1244/1274/1297 (the pool trampolines on a NULL opaque), none reachable from C. frame.rs lines are all covered; buffer.rs misses (695, 1118-1120) are wave-1 type batch 0 (UninitBuffer conversion refusal, a unit-test closure), outside this workset; BufferPoolUninit runs. The review adds tests/ub_safe/refstruct.rs::pool_teardown_in_callbacks (callbacks tearing their own pool down), which adds no line coverage but runs C paths no earlier test took: refstruct_pool_uninit and its free_entry flush nested in reset_cb, and pool_return_entry after uninit reached from inside a free_entry_cb.
